title: Stop trusting the query string
summary: GET /orders reads five filters off the query string and trusts them all: five orders on page two comes back with fifty, a typo in the page number comes back empty, and the one query it does refuse says only Bad Request. Put a schema in front of it.

checkpoints.title: The list pages, filters and sorts the way it was asked
checkpoints.hint: orders.list trusts whatever it is handed, and perPage reaches slice as its end offset: 5 + '5' is '55', so a page of five comes back fifty long. Hand it the values a caller meant rather than the ones that arrived.

checkpoints.title: The endpoint works from the parsed query, not the raw one
checkpoints.hint: Everything in req.query is a string, and 'false' is a truthy one. z.coerce.boolean() is Boolean(value), so it says true to both; z.stringbool() reads the string it was sent. safeParse puts the parsed query in .data, and that is the only copy worth passing on.

checkpoints.title: A query the endpoint cannot use never reaches the listing
checkpoints.hint: Number('abc') is NaN and nothing about that throws, so the check is the only thing that can refuse it. Answer and return: falling through to the listing after a 400 sends a second response. A schema that throws instead lands in Express's default error handler, which answers 500.

checkpoints.title: The 400 says which field, and what was wrong with it
checkpoints.hint: error.issues holds one entry per problem, each carrying a path and a message. Map all of them rather than issues[0], and path.join('.') is the parameter's name.
